items.title: In a first, ultrasound maps blood flow through an entire human kidney in 3D
items.text: For the first time, a research team at the Inserm Institute of Physics for Medicine (Inserm/ESPCI Paris-PSL/CNRS) in Paris has succeeded in visualizing the entire vascular network and blood flow in a human kidney. This breakthrough opens up promising clinical prospects: improving our understanding and diagnosis of kidney diseases linked to vascular defects. To achieve this, the researchers used a new ultrasound technique developed in their laboratory and previously tested in animals, which could eventually be extended to other organs. The results are published in The Lancet Medical Imaging & Theranostics.

To better treat these patients, scientists at the Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry (MPIP) collected comprehensive data on cell distributions and proteins from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples taken from patients with and without TRS.
